fixtures.title: Happy path — 14 brand logos
fixtures.purpose: 14 image-only links plus the label; enough to overflow the strip on desktop, so both arrows have work to do

fixtures.title: Below overflow — 2 brand logos
fixtures.purpose: The minimum that still classifies as a carousel, and few enough that nothing overflows

fixtures.title: Below threshold — 1 image link
fixtures.purpose: One image-only link, under the two-link rule, so no carousel should be built at all

fixtures.title: Captioned links — should not classify

fixtures.title: Hostile content

fixtures.title: Right-to-left — the strip in Arabic
fixtures.purpose: The brand strip authored in Arabic under ar-MA, inside an Arabic megamenu. The label is deliberately long — longer than any English equivalent — so the expansion case is a fixture a step can cite rather than something the tester has to author.

fixtures.title: Accessibility page
fixtures.purpose: Happy-path content on a page of its own, so tab order, screen-reader output and an axe scan describe the carousel and nothing else

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Authoring - Content model and classification
tests.scope: Whether the authored content produces a carousel at all: the label and tile row, the rule that classifies a strip of two or more image-only links as a brand carousel rather than featured products, and how the block degrades when an author omits the label or supplies a broken or oddly shaped image.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-01 and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The brand carousel renders with the "Our brands:" label and every authored logo shown as a round white tile in a single horizontal row.

steps.action: Count the tiles and compare against the links authored in the fixture's nav document.
steps.result: Exactly 8 tiles render, in the authored order, none missing and none duplicated.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-02 and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: Two logos still render as a brand carousel with the same structure as FX-01 — the block does not change shape because there are fewer items.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-03 and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: No brand carousel is built. A single image-only link is below the two-link threshold, and the panel renders without an empty carousel container left behind.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-04 and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The captioned image links render as featured products, not as a brand carousel — captions are what distinguish the two.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-05, which omits the label, and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: No labelless carousel renders. The label is a required slot, so the block does not present the strip as though the authored content were complete.

steps.action: In FX-05, find the tile whose image source is deliberately broken.
steps.result: The tile degrades gracefully — no broken-image icon, no collapsed tile, and the surrounding tiles keep their position and spacing.

steps.action: In FX-05, find the deliberately non-square logo.
steps.result: It is cropped to the round tile without stretching or squashing; the logo's aspect ratio is preserved.

steps.action: In FX-05, find the tile with very long alt text, and scroll the strip to its end.
steps.result: The long alt text does not widen the tile or break the row, and 24 logos scroll horizontally without breaking the panel or introducing page-level horizontal scrolling.

tests.notes: Step 6 is expected to fail. Gianluca Volpe clarified on 26 Aug 2026 that the label is required and that the code treating it as optional is a code issue; on develop FX-05 renders a carousel with no label at all. Two things still need writing down: AC-4 and AC-13 say the label can be left out, which now contradicts the answer, and nothing defines what should happen when an author omits a required slot. The step therefore asserts only that a labelless carousel is not presented as valid.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Functionality - Scrolling, arrows and megamenu stability
tests.scope: The carousel's runtime behaviour on a pointer device: arrow scrolling and the edge states that hide each arrow, wheel and trackpad scrolling, that operating the control never closes the megamenu, and that a tile navigates to its brand destination.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-01 on a desktop viewport and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The strip is at its start: the previous arrow is hidden and the next arrow is visible.

steps.action: Click the next arrow.
steps.result: The logo row scrolls smoothly toward the end, and the previous arrow becomes visible.

steps.action: Keep clicking next until the strip reaches its end.
steps.result: The next arrow is hidden at the end and the previous arrow remains visible. No further scrolling occurs.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-02, where all logos fit without overflowing, and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: Both arrows are hidden — there is nothing to scroll to.

steps.action: Return to FX-01 and scroll the logo row horizontally using a trackpad or mouse wheel.
steps.result: The row scrolls, and no scrollbar is visible at any point.

steps.action: Click either arrow and observe the megamenu.
steps.result: The Products megamenu stays open. Operating a control inside the carousel never dismisses the panel.

steps.action: Click the arrows rapidly and repeatedly, alternating directions.
steps.result: No stuck state, no duplicated or disappearing tiles, and arrow visibility still matches the strip position when the movement settles.

steps.action: Hover a tile with the pointer.
steps.result: The tile shows a subtle lift or shadow. Its neighbours do not shift position.

steps.action: Click a tile.
steps.result: The browser navigates to that brand's authored destination.

steps.action: Compare the behaviour observed on FX-01 and FX-02.
steps.result: The structure, controls and interaction model are identical in both. The one thing the number of logos changes is arrow visibility, which follows overflow as AC-8 requires.

tests.notes: AC-12 and AC-8 read as contradicting each other: AC-12 says changing the number of logos changes no behaviour, AC-8 says the arrows appear and disappear with overflow. Gianluca Volpe settled it on 26 Aug 2026 — keep AC-8. Step 10 asserts AC-12 as narrowed by that answer, and AC-12's own wording needs correcting to match.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Visual - Band, tiles, tokens and hover
tests.scope: How the carousel looks at a desktop reference viewport, measured against the handover design: the tinted band, the label's colour and overline treatment, arrow size and border, tile shape, and that nothing clips, overlaps or pushes the page sideways.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-01 at a 1440px-wide desktop viewport and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel sits at the bottom of the open panel as a full-width tinted band.

steps.action: Inspect the band's background colour.
steps.result: The band is #f5f3f4, matching the handover token.

steps.action: Inspect the "Our brands:" label at the start of the strip.
steps.result: The label is orange #d14900 and rendered in the uppercase overline style.

steps.action: Inspect the previous and next arrow buttons.
steps.data: Expected 40×40px, white, rounded square, #d14900 border and chevron
steps.result: Both arrows are 40×40px white rounded squares with an orange #d14900 border and chevron.

steps.action: Inspect the logo tiles.
steps.result: Each tile is a round white tile of consistent size, evenly spaced along a single row.

steps.action: Hover a tile and observe the effect against the band.
steps.result: The lift or shadow reads clearly against #f5f3f4 without the tile appearing detached or clipped by the band.

steps.action: Repeat at 1280px and 1200px viewport widths.
steps.result: No clipping, no overlap with the category columns above, and the band still spans the full panel width.

steps.action: At each width, check the document for horizontal overflow.
steps.result: The page itself never scrolls horizontally. The carousel's own internal scrolling is expected and is not page-level overflow.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-05, which omits the label, at 1440px.
steps.result: The strip starts at the band's leading edge with no reserved gap, and the band's height and alignment are unchanged.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Compatibility - Desktop layout and arrow behaviour
tests.scope: The desktop half of a block that is designed differently per viewport: where the carousel sits in the panel, that arrows exist and behave at the edges, and that crossing the breakpoint switches into and out of this layout without losing logos.
tests.notes: Steps 5 and 6 are expected to fail on develop. The header there switches layout at 1200px where the spec specifies 900px, so the desktop layout persists between 900px and 1199px. That is a defect in develop's header.css, not a fault in this test — raise it rather than re-running for a pass.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-01 at a desktop viewport above the breakpoint and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel renders at the bottom of the panel, below the category columns, as a full-width tinted band.

steps.action: Confirm the arrow controls are present.
steps.result: Previous and next arrows render at the ends of the strip.

steps.action: Operate both arrows to each end of the strip.
steps.result: Each arrow hides at the end it would scroll past, and the opposite arrow remains available.

steps.action: Compare position, spacing, typography and tile styling against the approved handover design for desktop.
steps.result: All match the handover for the desktop layout.

steps.action: Slowly resize the viewport downward across 900px with the megamenu open.
steps.data: The spec names 900px as the switch point
steps.result: At 900px the carousel switches to the mobile layout — moving to the top of the Products section and dropping its arrows — with every logo preserved, none lost and none duplicated.

steps.action: Resize back upward across 900px.
steps.result: The desktop layout returns, the band and arrows reappear, and arrow visibility is recomputed correctly for the current scroll position.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Compatibility - Mobile layout and swipe behaviour
tests.scope: The mobile half of the same block, which is a different design rather than a smaller one: the carousel moves above the category columns, loses its band and arrows entirely, and is driven by swipe alone.
tests.notes: Step 6 shares the breakpoint defect described on BRANDS-TC-04 — on develop the switch happens at 1200px rather than the specified 900px. Step 2 asserts the separator below the strip rather than above it as AC-3 says: Gianluca Volpe's answer of 26 Aug 2026 is to follow the designs, and the handover prototype draws it below. AC-3 needs correcting to match.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-01 on a mobile viewport, open the navigation drawer and expand the Products section.
steps.result: The brand carousel appears at the top of the Products section, above the category columns.

steps.action: Inspect the label and the separator.
steps.result: The "Our brands:" label sits on top of the logo row, with a hairline separator below the strip and a transparent background — no tinted band.

steps.action: Look for arrow controls.
steps.result: No arrow buttons are present anywhere in the mobile carousel.

steps.action: Swipe the logo row horizontally.
steps.result: The row scrolls with the swipe, and no scrollbar is visible.

steps.action: Compare position, spacing, typography and tile styling against the approved handover design for mobile.
steps.result: All match the handover for the mobile layout.

steps.action: Resize the viewport upward across 900px with the drawer open.
steps.result: The layout switches to desktop — the carousel moves to the bottom of the panel, gains its tinted band and arrows — with every logo preserved.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Accessibility - Keyboard, semantics and contrast
tests.scope: WCAG 2.1 AA for the carousel: that a keyboard user can enter, operate and leave it without trapping, that every control is reachable and named, and that the label, arrow border and chevron meet contrast against the band they sit on.
tests.notes: Step 8 is expected to fail on current code. The label measures #d14900 on #f5f3f4 at 12px weight 600, which computes to 4.08:1 against the 4.5:1 required for normal text. Raise it as a defect rather than re-running. Step 4 is a known risk area: the focus indicator on a tile, and the behaviour of an arrow that hides while it holds focus.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-07 on a desktop viewport, open the Products megamenu, and Tab forward until focus enters the carousel.
steps.result: Focus reaches the carousel in a logical reading order, after the category columns.

steps.action: Continue tabbing through the carousel.
steps.result: Every logo tile and both arrow buttons are reachable, in the order they appear on screen.

steps.action: With a tile focused, press Enter. Then focus an arrow and press Space.
steps.result: Enter activates the focused tile link; Space activates the focused arrow button. Note that links activate on Enter only — Space is for buttons.

steps.action: Observe the focus indicator on a tile, then on an arrow, and scroll so a focused arrow reaches the edge where it hides.
steps.result: A visible focus ring is shown against the band at every stop, and focus is never left on a control that has been hidden.

steps.action: Keep tabbing past the last control, then Shift-Tab back out the way you came.
steps.result: Focus leaves the carousel in both directions using the keyboard alone. There is no keyboard trap.

steps.action: Inspect the accessible name of each logo link with a screen reader or the accessibility inspector.
steps.result: Each link takes its accessible name from the image's alt text and identifies the brand.

steps.action: Inspect the accessible name and markup of each arrow.
steps.result: The previous arrow is labelled "Previous brands" and the next "Next brands", and each chevron is aria-hidden so it is not announced separately.

steps.action: Measure the contrast of the label against the band.
steps.data: Label #d14900 on band #f5f3f4; AA requires 4.5:1 for normal text
steps.result: The ratio is at least 4.5:1.

steps.action: Measure the contrast of the arrow border and chevron against their backgrounds.
steps.data: AA requires 3:1 for non-text UI components and graphical objects
steps.result: Both meet at least 3:1.

steps.action: Run axe-core against the page with the megamenu open, then run a Lighthouse accessibility audit.
steps.result: axe reports no new violations attributable to the carousel, and the Lighthouse accessibility score is 100 barring pre-existing issues elsewhere on the page.

tests.summary: Header: Products Brand Carousel - Internationalization - RTL mirroring and text expansion
tests.scope: That the carousel works in a right-to-left locale and with longer translated text. The fixture is authored in Arabic rather than mirrored English, so what a reviewer sees is what an Arabic market would see; its strip label is also the longest of any locale we test, which covers expansion without asking anyone to edit content.
tests.notes:
EC-14 states no acceptance criterion for RTL or localisation. This test exists under the agent's mandatory-coverage rule, not derived from the ticket — see Coverage gaps.

RTL is reached by page metadata: decorateLocale() in scripts.js reads a Language or Locale row and sets lang and dir on <html>, so FX-06 carries Language: ar-MA. header.css is written with logical properties throughout (inset-inline, margin-inline, padding-inline, border-inline) and no physical margin-left/right, so most mirroring should happen by construction. The residual risk is 4 left: and 3 right: declarations that remain physical — step 3 targets those.

steps.action: Open fixture FX-06 on a right-to-left page at a desktop viewport and open the Products megamenu.
steps.result: The carousel mirrors: the label — "تعرّف على علاماتنا التجارية العالمية:" — sits at the right-hand end of the strip and the logo row begins from the right.

steps.action: Confirm the document direction is applied.
steps.result: The page carries dir="rtl" and the corresponding lang attribute for the locale.

steps.action: Locate the previous and next arrows.
steps.result: The arrows are mirrored: the control that advances through the logos sits on the left, and its chevron points left.

steps.action: Operate the arrow that advances through the strip.
steps.result: The row scrolls toward the logical end of the list, not toward the visual right.

steps.action: Inspect the accessible names of both arrows.
steps.result: The names describe logical direction rather than visual left and right — "previous" and "next", not "left" and "right". Record whether they are localised: if they read as English on an Arabic page they are hardcoded in the block and cannot be translated, which is a finding in itself.

steps.action: Read the strip's label, which is the longest translation we hold, and check it against the logo row.
steps.result: The label renders in full. It does not clip, wrap awkwardly, overlap the logo row, or push the strip into page-level horizontal scrolling. The logos keep their size and spacing.
